info.text: A script that ran once is not yet a reproducible analysis. Reproduction depends on identified inputs, explicit parameters, versioned software and reference data, recorded execution, validated outputs, and enough provenance to explain every result.

clusters.name: Defining an analysis
clusters.fact: A reproducible analysis begins with an explicit input manifest, parameter set, reference dataset, and quality-control criteria rather than relying on filenames and remembered defaults.

input manifest.text: A structured inventory connecting sample identifiers with the files and attributes supplied to a run.

parameter set.text: The explicit configuration values and thresholds supplied to tools in an analysis.

reference dataset.text: A versioned external sequence, annotation, or database used as a comparison or interpretation resource.

quality-control checkpoint.text: A defined test and acceptance rule applied before downstream analysis proceeds or results are accepted.

clusters.name: Fixing the software environment
clusters.fact: Pinned dependency versions and environment lockfiles identify software, while a versioned container image captures a fuller runtime environment.

dependency version.text: The precise release or revision of a tool or library required by an analysis.

environment lockfile.text: A machine-readable record that resolves requested software dependencies to exact versions or artifacts.

container image.text: A versioned package of filesystem and runtime dependencies used to create consistent execution environments.

clusters.name: Orchestrating execution
clusters.fact: A workflow definition connects tasks; task dependencies establish order, resource declarations expose computational needs, and retry policy defines how selected failures are handled.

workflow definition.text: A machine-readable description of analysis tasks, dependencies, inputs, outputs, and execution rules.

task dependency.text: A declared relationship requiring one task or its outputs to be ready before another task can run.

compute resource.text: Declared CPU, memory, storage, accelerator, or scheduling requirements for a task.

retry policy.text: A rule specifying which failed tasks may be attempted again, how often, and under what conditions.

clusters.name: Recording what happened
clusters.fact: Run logs record execution, checksums verify artifact identity, intermediate outputs support diagnosis, and a results manifest identifies the products delivered by a particular run.

run log.text: A timestamped record of commands, status, warnings, errors, and other events from an execution.

checksum.text: A digest calculated from data and used to detect whether an artifact's bytes differ.

intermediate artifact.text: A file or dataset produced between final endpoints that can support caching, inspection, and fault diagnosis.

results manifest.text: A structured inventory of the outputs, identifiers, and integrity information associated with a completed run.

bridges.fact: A workflow engine interprets the declared analysis graph, schedules ready tasks, passes identified inputs and parameters, and manages failures or retries on available resources.

info.text: Software that resolves task dependencies and coordinates execution of a computational workflow.

bridges.fact: Version control connects analysis intent to implementation history by preserving changes to workflow definitions, configuration, and supporting code—though large data artifacts need separate versioning strategies.

info.text: A system for recording and identifying changes to files such as code, workflow definitions, and configuration.

bridges.fact: Provenance joins declared inputs and parameters, the software and environment actually executed, and the artifacts produced into an inspectable lineage for each result.

info.text: Structured lineage describing the entities, activities, software, and relationships that produced a data result.

lenses.prompt: Which concepts identify the data and computational choices needed to repeat the same analysis?
lenses.explanation: Inputs, parameters, references, dependencies, and runtime environments must be identifiable; checksums help verify that named artifacts are actually the same bytes.

reasons.input manifest: It enumerates the samples and files entering a run.
reasons.parameter set: It records choices that can alter tool behavior and results.
reasons.reference dataset: Its exact release or build can change coordinates and annotations.
reasons.dependency version: Different software releases can implement different behavior.
reasons.container image: It packages a defined execution environment more completely than a tool name alone.
reasons.checksum: It verifies artifact identity at the byte level.

lenses.prompt: Which concepts show why merely automating commands is insufficient for reproducibility?
lenses.explanation: Automation specifies steps, but reproduction also needs the software and data identities, execution record, integrity checks, lineage, and explicit criteria that determine whether a run is acceptable.

reasons.workflow definition: It describes the dependency graph and commands but may not pin everything they use.
reasons.dependency version: Unpinned software can make the same commands behave differently.
reasons.run log: It records what actually happened rather than only what was intended.
reasons.checksum: It detects silent substitution or corruption of an artifact.
reasons.provenance: It connects each output to the inputs and transformations that produced it.
reasons.quality-control checkpoint: It makes acceptance criteria part of the process rather than an undocumented judgment.

lenses.prompt: Which concepts help locate why two nominally identical runs produced different outputs?
lenses.explanation: Differences can arise from parameters, reference releases, software, resource-dependent execution, failures visible in logs, or simply comparing different output sets. These records localize the divergence.

reasons.parameter set: It reveals configuration differences between runs.
reasons.reference dataset: It identifies changes in external biological knowledge or coordinates.
reasons.compute resource: Threads, memory, hardware, or distributed scheduling can affect some tools.
reasons.run log: It reveals warnings, retries, failures, and executed commands.
reasons.results manifest: It states exactly which outputs are being compared.

lenses.prompt: Which concepts distinguish what an analysis was instructed to do from the record of what it actually produced?
lenses.explanation: Manifests, parameters, and workflow definitions declare intended inputs and work. Logs and artifacts record the realized execution, while the results manifest identifies the outputs that actually emerged.

reasons.input manifest: It declares the samples and files intended to enter a run.
reasons.parameter set: It declares the configuration intended to govern tool behavior.
reasons.workflow definition: It declares tasks and their dependency structure.
reasons.run log: It records execution events, warnings, and failures that actually occurred.
reasons.intermediate artifact: It is tangible evidence produced during execution.
reasons.results manifest: It inventories the outputs associated with the completed run.
